title: Data & Research Administrator
description:
Key Responsibilities:
- Provide day-to-day administrative and data support to the Investment/Research team, acting as an assistant to colleagues across a range of recurring and ad hoc tasks.
- Extract data from internal and external sources and prepare it for use in reporting, analysis and operational processes.
- Clean, organise, reconcile and manipulate data in Excel, including combining datasets, identifying inconsistencies and resolving data-quality issues.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records, databases, spreadsheets and reporting tools, ensuring information is complete, consistent and available when required.
- Produce regular and ad hoc reports, schedules and data summaries for internal stakeholders, following established templates and procedures.
- Carry out data checks and reconciliations, investigate exceptions and follow up missing or inaccurate information with the appropriate team members.
- Review existing administrative and data processes, identify inefficiencies or control gaps, and suggest practical improvements to make processes more accurate, consistent and efficient.

Skills & Experience:
- Advanced Excel skills are essential, with confidence using formulas, lookups, PivotTables, filters, sorting and other tools to extract, clean and manipulate data.
- Strong numerical and analytical ability, with the confidence to work with large volumes of data and identify errors, trends and inconsistencies.
- Experience in a data administration, reporting, operations, record-keeping or similar support role is preferred; financial services experience is useful but not essential.
- No specific finance degree or professional finance qualification is required; practical data-handling ability, accuracy and strong Excel skills are more important.
- Excellent attention to detail, organisation and time-management skills, with a methodical approach to maintaining records and completing recurring tasks.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to ask questions, follow up information and work effectively with colleagues across the business.

Key Attributes:
- Highly organised, dependable and comfortable working in a support-focused role with multiple routine and ad hoc priorities.
- Methodical and data-focused, with a strong commitment to accuracy, completeness and good record keeping.
- Curious about how processes work and willing to question, document and improve existing ways of working.
- Collaborative and service-oriented, with a practical approach to supporting the wider team and meeting deadlines.

title: Sales Support Administrator
description:
Job Title: Sales Support Administrator

Salary: 26,500

Location: Northwich

Our client is currently looking to expand their team and hire an additional sales support administrator. An excellent opportunity to join a growing organisation that prides themself on delivering a first class services to their ever expanding client base. This role is supporting the key account managers, been the first point of contact for customers regarding product information, processing orders etc.

Main Duties:

Collaborate with Account Managers to provide pre and post-sales support, ensuring seamless customer experiences.

Source solutions and engage with suppliers for run rate products / software / services.

Provide accurate quotes to customers.

Act as a key point of contact and ensure orders are processed accurately and in line with contractual SLAs.

Engage with clients to gather feedback, address inquiries, and provide solutions.

Monitor and expedite client orders to ensure delivery within client SLAs, resolving any delivery issues ensuring the customer is informed as appropriate.

Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of customer interactions in our CRM system.

Ensure compliance with internal best practice processes.

Work in collaboration with internal departments such as finance, logistics, sales and purchasing.

To undertake additional duties that may be required from time to time.

INDAB

title: Call Centre Agent - Uncapped Commission
description:
Start Date: 05/10/2026

Full Time Role - 37.5 hours per week

Stanford House Birchwood WA3 7 TH

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our team in Warrington is full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Warrington contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE
- GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.
- UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.
- BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.
- GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.
- FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.
- GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

title: Bank Administrator
description: As a Bank Administrative Assistant in Contraception and Sexual Health, youll be working as part of the care system in Cheshire West and Chester. You will feel valued as a Bank Administration Assistant within HCRG Care Group, receiving access to exclusive rewards and benefits including: £12.71 an hour, Self-booking and access to all bank shifts! Staff are given access to all Bank shifts within their Business Unit and can self-book providing they meet the shift requirements. Request a Duty Staff can make shifts or Day Off requests prior to the creation of a roster up to six weeks in advance. This helps promote a better work life balance and allows for personal commitments to be met. HCRG Care Group is pleased to offer access to Wagestream - which lets you track your pay throughout the month and stream your earned wages into your bank account if you need them. No more high-interest loans or overdraft fees - simply get paid as you go. Working in an environment focused on the highest clinical and quality standards. Opportunities to work in different areas and various different services to gain new knowledge and experience. As a Bank Administrative Assistant in Contraception and Sexual Health, you will work as part of the care system in Cheshire West and Chester. You will perform reception duties, update patient personal details, manage follow-up appointments, and maintain patient case notes. Your role includes ensuring accurate patient demographics, handling telephone enquiries politely, supporting negative results communication, and maintaining filing systems. You will also perform basic copy typing, manage incoming mail, and work across several locations in Cheshire. Benefits include £12.71 per hour, self-booking shifts, request a duty, Wagestream access, highest clinical standards environment, development opportunities, and access to professional networks. You will also get free training, a well-being service, and opportunities for innovation. The role requires a full UK driving licence and access to a car. You will be encouraged to apply for national funding to drive your initiatives locally to benefit our patients and service users Rewarding and supportive teams , you will be recognised and have opportunities to recognise others by nominating for local and national awards annually and taking part in our new virtual Ask our Executives event, where you can submit questions to the board and hear updates regularly on company strategy and objectives The pride of working for an organisation committed to the highest clinical and quality standards: with a majority of our rated services holding good or outstanding ratings from the Care Quality Commission Working directly with our multi disciplinary team you will assist the administration team with daily tasks, demonstrate excellent IT and workload management skills, provide exceptional customer service skills on reception and over the phone, order and take deliveries, and flexibility in supporting other teams and administration assistants. As a Bank Administration Assistant you will: Undertake reception duties, including updating patients personal details and organising follow-up appointments or add patient to an outpatient waiting list following a standard operational procedure. Create, update and amend patient case notes as required, particularly in respect of ensuring all patient demographics are accurate as required. Ensure telephone enquiries are dealt with in a polite and courteous manner. Support with negative results and patient communication. Undertake photocopying, facsimiles, email, memo requests and basic ad-hoc copy typing if required. Maintain a filing system for any hard copy records, ensure electronic records are maintained in line with local policy and guidelines. Sort and distribute and action incoming mail if required. You will be required to work across a multiple of location throughout Cheshire West and Chester that includes but not limitedto:Chester, Ellesmere Port, Northwich, Winsford, Neston and Blacon Please see the attached job description for a full list of job responsibilities. We are looking for candidate who meets the following criteria: Has a full UK driving licence and access to a car Recent experience working in an administrative or customer service role Familiar with IT systems Has worked in the NHS / healthcare (desirable) Please note that this advert may close early if a sufficient number of applications are received. About the Company We change lives by transforming health and care. Established in 2006 we are one of the UK's leading independent providers of community health and care services, working with health and care commissioners and communities to transform services with a focus on experience, efficiency and improved outcomes. We deliver and transform adult and children community health services, primary care services including urgent care, sexual health, dermatology and MSK services as well as adult social care and wellbeing services.Across England, we support communities of many millions and directly help more than half a million people each year - guided by our simple values: we care, we think, we do. We're committed to equal opportunities and welcome applications from a broad, diverse range of people who want to join our team.Were a Disability Confident Committed company, so we work to provide facilities, work environment adjustments and technical solutions to be as inclusive of everyone. While it doesnt happen often, sometimes a role is very popular, and well need to close it earlier than the date weve shown here. If youre keen to join our team, wed love to hear from you so please apply as soon as you can. As youd expect, safeguarding and protecting the children, young people and vulnerable adults that we work with is of the utmost importance so we have policies and procedures in place to promote safeguarding and safer working practices and everyone who joins the team is subject to a safer recruitment process, including the disclosure of criminal records and vetting checks. Finally, we need to let you know that the company youll work for is part of HCRG Care Group Holdings Limited and by applying for this job well need to process and hold information about you. If you would like to know a little more about how we use your information, please see our website's privacy policy.
